title: Gender and Diversity in Psychiatric Care
summary:
Mental illness affects many people, but not everyone in the same way. Gender, origin, social status, and living conditions influence how individuals develop mental illnesses, what treatments they receive, and how effective those treatments are. Nevertheless, these differences have so far been scarcely incorporated into psychiatric care in a systematic way.
The PSY-DIVER project addresses this issue and investigates how patients can be viewed and treated in a more individualized, gender-sensitive, and diversity-sensitive manner in the future. To this end, data from a large network of psychiatric hospitals with approximately 50,000 inpatient and 170,000 outpatient cases annually is being utilized. The study specifically examines differences in medication, therapies used, and treatment outcomes based on factors such as gender, origin, living situation, or other characteristics. Additionally, patients, family members, and healthcare professionals are interviewed to better understand their experiences and needs. The goal is psychiatric care that takes all people into account.
The project uses a so-called mixed-methods design. This combines the analysis of large data sets with personal interviews. Artificial intelligence is used to extract additional information from digital medical records. At the same time, personal perspectives are incorporated through interviews and questionnaires. In a structured participatory process, the results are ultimately evaluated together with mental illness-affected individuals and experts, and recommendations for action are developed.
The project is receiving funding of approximately one million euros over three years.
The recommendations for action will help make psychiatric care more equitable, personalized, and effective in the future—for all patients, regardless of their gender or social background.
conditions: Persons with mental illness and psychiatric treatment experience, relatives/close ones of persons with mental illness and psychiatric treatment experience, clinical professionals

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Subproject 1 (Routine data analyses): For the analyses, all cases of patients from the LVR Clinical Group Department with a discharge date between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024, will initially be used. Over the course of the project, the analysis period will be expanded to ensure greater timeliness, so that (exclusively retrospective) data from the years 2025, 2026, 2027, and 2028 can also be used successively.

Subproject 2 (Surveys): 
1. Minimum age of 18;
2. Presence of a (chronic) mental illness and current or past psychiatric-psychotherapeutic treatment, or the presence of such a person in the respondent’s immediate, close personal circle, or professional activity in psychiatric-psychotherapeutic care; 
3. Sufficient German language skills to understand and answer the interview questions or the questionnaire.
Exclusion criteria:
Subproject 1: None; this is a census study. 
Subproject 2: 
1. Acute risk to self or others that precludes participation in the study.
2. Severe cognitive impairment or delirium that makes informed consent impossible.
